_readme: A real, shared bug-tracking schema for the deep-dive testing pass — designed to hand off cleanly between you and Copilot, so both of you are filling in and reading the exact same structure rather than two different mental models of what a 'bug report' looks like.

_schema.id: Short, unique string. Suggested pattern: BUG-001, BUG-002, etc. — sequential, so nothing gets silently overwritten.
_schema.title: One-line summary — what you'd say out loud if someone asked 'what's wrong'.
_schema.whatsHappening: The actual, observed behavior. Be concrete: not 'the panel is broken', but 'clicking Save closes the panel without writing to localStorage'.
_schema.whereInApplication: The real, specific location — which OmniProduct/panel/menu, and the real file if you know it (e.g. 'OmniTranslator, Left vault' or 'ui/OmniJsonifier.js, theme picker'). This is the field that saves the most real back-and-forth time later.
_schema.desiredOutcome: What should happen instead — stated as the real, correct behavior, not just 'fix it'.
_schema.severity: One of: blocking | high | medium | low | cosmetic. blocking = can't test past this point. cosmetic = visual only, nothing breaks.
_schema.status: One of: untested | confirmed | in-progress | fixed | wontfix. Starts at 'confirmed' the moment you've actually seen it happen once.
_schema.stepsToReproduce: Optional but genuinely valuable — a real, numbered list. Skip only if it's a one-glance visual issue.
_schema.foundBy: Who found it — you, or noted during a Copilot session.
_schema.assignedTo: Who's actually working the fix — you, Copilot, or Claude (this session).
_schema.notes: Freeform — anything that doesn't fit the fields above. Screenshots, related bug ids, a hunch about the real cause.
